## Prepare for the coding interview.

Learn the subjects, practise against the clock and sit realistic interview rounds before the real one. Visual courses, notes, videos, practice sheets, aptitude mocks and AI interviews, all on one account.

Your week

Placement prep, week 3

3 of 5 done

1. MonTCP, the three-way handshakeLearn · Networking, illustrated chapter
2. TueSliding window sheetPractise · 6 problems, C++ and Java
3. WedAptitude mock, quantitativePractise · 30 questions, 30 minutes
4. ThuIndexes and B+ treesLearn · Databases, with your notesToday
5. FriSystem design roundInterview · Link shortener, 45 min

Last debrief · Code review · 4 of 5

## Learn it, practise it, then sit the round.

Interview preparation is usually spread across a dozen tabs. Here it follows one path, and your progress, notes and streak come with you at every step.

## Notes that read like a good teacher drew them for you.

Networking, operating systems and databases, explained one hand-drawn page at a time. Every chapter is written with interviews in mind: what it is, why it matters, and how it comes up.

## Sit the round before the round.

Four rounds modelled on how companies interview today. Each one ends with a written debrief that quotes your own work back to you, so you know exactly what to improve.

## A plan that fits the time you actually have.

Tell us what you want to learn and how many days you have. You get a syllabus sized to your level, in an order that makes sense, and one clear list for each day. Miss a day and it simply moves to your backlog.

- Any subject, from linked lists to system design
- Algorithm tasks open straight into the visual lesson
- One short list each morning, nothing to manage

## Prepare a whole batch, not one student at a time.

Placement cells use Chai Prep to get final-year students ready and run practice drives. Companies use it to onboard graduate hires and assess them before day one. You get your own portal; we handle the platform.

- Bring everyone in at once
	Import your roster, assign seats and see who has joined and who needs a nudge.
- Run drives on your schedule
	Aptitude, coding and code review rounds, one link for everyone, make-up windows built in.
- Fair by design
	Papers drawn fresh for each round. Focus changes and pastes recorded, with no camera.
- Results you can act on
	Ranked lists and score spreads, so you see who is ready and who needs more practice.

## Good to know.

Is Chai Prep free?

You can start for free. The first DSA track, the video courses and the practice sheets are open to everyone. One plan, from ₹499 a month, unlocks every course, aptitude mock and roadmap. AI interviews are bought separately, from ₹99 each.

What happened to Chai Visual?

It grew. Chai Visual started as animated DSA lessons, and those are all still here as the visual courses. Chai Prep is the name for everything around them now: notes, videos, practice, mocks and interviews.

Who is it for?

Students preparing for placements, engineers getting ready to switch jobs, and colleges or companies preparing a whole batch together.

How are the AI interviews marked?

Every round is marked against a written rubric for that problem. Your debrief explains each score and quotes the parts of your work it is based on, so the feedback is specific and easy to act on.

Do I need to install anything?

No. Everything runs in your browser, including the codebase and editor in the coding interview.

![](https://dsa.chaicode.com/_next/image?url=%2Fchai-mascot-dark.png&w=256&q=75)

## Start where you are. Walk in ready.

Open a lesson, solve a sheet or sit a practice round today. Everything you do here builds towards the same goal: your next interview.

## Good to know.

Is Chai Prep free?

You can start for free. The first DSA track, the video courses and the practice sheets are open to everyone. One plan, from ₹499 a month, unlocks every course, aptitude mock and roadmap. AI interviews are bought separately, from ₹99 each.

What happened to Chai Visual?

It grew. Chai Visual started as animated DSA lessons, and those are all still here as the visual courses. Chai Prep is the name for everything around them now: notes, videos, practice, mocks and interviews.

Who is it for?

Students preparing for placements, engineers getting ready to switch jobs, and colleges or companies preparing a whole batch together.

How are the AI interviews marked?

Every round is marked against a written rubric for that problem. Your debrief explains each score and quotes the parts of your work it is based on, so the feedback is specific and easy to act on.

Do I need to install anything?

No. Everything runs in your browser, including the codebase and editor in the coding interview.
